articles.title: George Lucas' Original Star Wars Sequel Plans Were Hated So Much By Disney Boss, He Changed the Lucasfilm Deal
articles.summary: These days, people look at the Star Wars franchise and all the divisiveness that comes with it as some sort of fall-off for the franchise. However, the truth is: Star Wars has been on a turbulent ride since the beginning, and it's continued through every era of the franchise, including Disney's acquisition of Lucasfilm in […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google These days, people look at the Star Wars franchise and all the divisiveness that comes with it as some sort of fall-off for the franchise. However, the truth is: Star Wars has been on a turbulent ride since the beginning, and it's continued through every era of the franchise, including Disney's acquisition of Lucasfilm in the mid-2010s. Now, some new insights about that pivotal time in Star Wars are coming to light, and it looks like George Lucas hit a wall of divisiveness so thick that he risked blowing up the deal.

A new book from Wall Street Journal reporter/author Robbie Whelan is about to hit bookshelves. Titled The House of Mouse: Bob Iger and the War of Succession at Disney , the book will reveal new insights about the inner workings at Disney as Bob Iger joined the company, rose to the top spot of CEO, retired, only to un-retire and snatch the reins back from his own successor, Bob Chapek, after Chapek led Disney down some ruinous paths.

One major focus of the book is how Iger pulled off the unimaginable move of expanding Disney's brand and core customer base to include just as many boys as there are girl fans living out princess dreams. Iger brought Lucasfilm, Marvel, and 21st Century Fox into the Disney tent and also reunited Disney with Pixar. During his podcast show The Town, host Matthew Belloni interviewed Robbie Whelan and had to ask about one specific anecdote in the book: Bob Iger's reaction to George Lucas's original scripts for Episodes VIII, IX, and X, aka "the sequel trilogy."

As Belloni recounts: "Lucas actually had treatments for three Star Wars movies that he wanted Disney to make after the acquisition. You write this in the book: 'After reading the plot outlines, Iger decided Disney had to buy them, but he made sure to write into the contract that Disney had no legal obligation to actually make the movies. Another person who was involved in the negotiation recalls that Iger hated the treatments and said privately, 'We are not making these movies,' [laughter]. How bad were they?"

Whelan was very diplomatic in his answer, wisely keeping the talk focused on his main subject (Iger), instead of badmouthing George Lucas: "Imagine you're an executive who's never written a movie, never directed a movie, and George Lucas sends you a package of scripts, and you look at these and say, 'This is terrible. We're never making this.'"

That statement lets all the context around it speak volumes. Belloni addresses it in his follow-up, saying that after the prequel trilogy, there was very little confidence in George Lucas as a writer/director – apparently with good reason . Lucas hasn't directed a film since Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith , and at age 80+, it will likely be his final work.

As for Iger: the karmic joke ended up being on him, as the Star Wars sequel trilogy he did approve of went from a record-shattering first film to splitting fans far apart with the second film ( The Last Jedi ) and uniting everyone in disappointment with the third ( The Rise of Skywalker ). Maybe ol' George wasn't so crazy after all…

You can stream all Star Wars movies on Disney+.

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero's Sequel Needs to Give Players More Main Weapons and Fewer Phantom Edges
articles.summary: Courtesy of S-GAME Studio Phantom Blade Zero has a habit of putting the coolest weapons imaginable into the hands of people who desperately want to kill you. One moment, you're locked in a spectacular duel against some impossibly stylish warrior. The next, you're watching them unleash a weapon so absurdly cool that your immediate reaction is "I NEED THAT […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Phantom Blade Zero has a habit of putting the coolest weapons imaginable into the hands of people who desperately want to kill you. One moment, you're locked in a spectacular duel against some impossibly stylish warrior. The next, you're watching them unleash a weapon so absurdly cool that your immediate reaction is "I NEED THAT THING." It's one of the game's greatest strengths. Unfortunately, that excitement sometimes comes with a rather disappointing catch: you might get the weapon, but not in the way you hoped.

Phantom Blade Zero splits its arsenal between main weapons and Phantom Edges, the latter serving as supplemental combat abilities rather than full-fledged weapons. It's a cool system that gives players plenty of ways to get creative during fights, but it also means some of the game's most spectacular weapon designs never get the chance to become the stars of their own movesets. Truly a missed opportunity. If S-Game ever gives us a sequel, I want to see more of those weapons promoted into the main arsenal. There are too many incredible designs here to leave some of them playing second fiddle.

One of the smartest things about Phantom Blade Zero is how it separates its two weapon systems. Main weapons form the foundation of a player's combat style, with two slots allowing you to switch between different approaches as a fight unfolds. Phantom Edges offer another layer of expression through powerful supplemental attacks. It's a satisfying arrangement because it gives combat plenty of room to breathe without turning every encounter into a chaotic button-mashing contest. The problem is that the distinction can sometimes feel more restrictive than it needs to be. When a Phantom Edge has a design that could easily support an entire moveset, limiting it to a secondary ability feels like leaving an excellent idea only half-finished.

This becomes especially noticeable when bosses enter the picture. Phantom Blade Zero knows how to make a weapon feel like an extension of its wielder, and some of the most memorable encounters are elevated by the sheer spectacle of watching an enemy unleash a distinctive fighting style. Naturally, that makes players want to get their hands on the same weapon. It's a core part of the appeal that S-game setup: fight a boss, get their weapon. Sadly, while you do often get the weapon, discovering that a particularly exciting design is only available as a Phantom Edge can feel like being handed the wrapping paper after someone else gets the present.

To be clear, the concept of Phantom Edges aren't the problem. They're a great way to give additional options without requiring every new weapon to become another full-fledged addition to the main arsenal. But that flexibility should work both ways. Some designs deserve to remain supplemental abilities while others could become the centerpiece of an entirely new fighting style. The distinction shouldn't be determined solely by which category a weapon happens to occupy. If a design has enough personality to make an enemy encounter memorable, there's a good chance it has enough potential to become a fantastic main weapon, too. I'd love to see S-Game recognize that opportunity rather than leave some of its most exciting creations confined to a single combat function.

I absolutely want S-Game to keep expanding the arsenal in a sequel. In fact, I'd love to see even more outlandish weapon designs that make players rethink how they approach combat. There's so much potential in Phantom Blade Zero 's martial arts fantasy that limiting the next game's weapon roster to familiar blades would be a huge missed opportunity. Give us stranger weapons. Give us something that looks completely ridiculous until we see what it can do in the hands of a skilled fighter. Most importantly, give us the opportunity to actually master those weapons rather than relegating so many of them to the Phantom Edge system.

Take the Thunder Spear, for example. Getting this weapon is genuinely exciting, especially when you consider how much potential it has as part of the main arsenal. Then comes the realization that it's a Phantom Edge. Really? Instead of getting an entirely new moveset to learn and incorporate into your fighting style, you're left with a single ability that consumes a resource on one of the most spectualr looking weapons in the game. It is still a useful addition to combat, but it isn't nearly as exciting as having the weapon available as one of your primary choices. I wanted to fight with the Thunder Spear, not simply borrow it for one attack before returning to my regular weapons. It's difficult not to imagine how much more interesting it could have been with a full moveset.

Phantom Edges have a place in the combat system, and I wouldn't want to lose the extra flexibility they provide. However, the sequel should be more willing to turn its coolest weapon concepts into fully playable additions to the main arsenal. Keep introducing new designs and keep surprising players with the things they can wield. Just don't let so many of those fantastic ideas end up as a single resource-consuming ability when they could have been an entirely new fighting style. There's a world of difference between briefly unleashing a weapon's power and actually learning to master it. I know which one I'd rather have.

Which Phantom Edge would you most like to see become a main weapon? Are there any weapons you think are better suited to the Phantom Edge system? Let us know in the comments below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new anime just confirmed its 2027 release window, and action fantasy fans must add it to their watchlist. 2026 is almost finally its end, which is why the next year’s lineup is revealing all the major information fans can expect. Looking at the lineup, it's evident that 2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season , which is only a few weeks away, but a lot of the incredible series will be released throughout the year.

It goes without saying that action fantasy fans have a lot to look forward to this year, including a new upcoming series, Shozen . The anime is based on a Chinese web comic, but despite the fact that it's pretty underrated internationally, the anime is grabbing attention thanks to its unique premise and stunning visuals. While the anime was announced earlier this year, the official X handle finally reveals the release window along with a gorgeous visual. Additionally, the official YouTube channel of Fuji TV Anime shared the second promotional trailer, which includes the broadcast information and the staff members.

The anime is scheduled to be released in April 2027 as part of the Spring lineup. However, the exact release date will only be announced a few weeks before the premiere. So far, the anime has only revealed that it will broadcast on Fuji TV’s B8station and Japanese TV networks. The broadcast dates and timings will also be shared at a later date. The official handle also confirms that the broadcast schedule can change without notice during its airing. The anime has yet to confirm its streaming platform, so there's no guarantee when global fans will be able to watch it. As the largest streaming service across the world, Crunchyroll has the highest possibility of acquiring the rights to the anime, but we can't say for certain before the platform reveals its Spring 2027 lineup.

The story begins with a Taoist priest wandering across the land to track down a demon. However, he never could have imagined that his target would be raising a human girl in the middle of a forest. Since the girl grew up eating demons, her body has changed significantly, even to the point that the food from the human world isn't enough to keep her alive. On the other hand, the demon has given up on taking care of her because of an impending heavenly tribulation. Seeing that the girl has nowhere else to go, the priest takes her under his wing and gives her the Taoist name Shangshan.

The anime follows their journey as master and disciple while they encounter countless challenges ahead. The premise is certainly one of a kind , as it's something you don't really come across. Not to mention that the visuals breathe life into the exceptional storytelling and the characters. So far, the anime looks incredibly promising, but we will have to wait until the premiere to see if it meets expectations.

articles.title: One of the Best Stephen King Adaptations is Leaving Netflix Sooner Than You Think
articles.summary: Stephen King adaptations have been having a great run as of late. Movies like The Running Man, The Long Walk, and The Life of Chuck all were well-received last year. HBO Max’s It: Welcome to Derry has been a hit and a second is on the way and, most recently Prime Video’s Carrie has also […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Stephen King adaptations have been having a great run as of late. Movies like The Running Man , The Long Walk , and The Life of Chuck all were well-received last yea r. HBO Max’s It: Welcome to Derry has been a hit and a second is on the way and, most recently Prime Video’s Carrie has also gone over well with critics and audiences alike. But for as great as it has been to be a King fan this year, there is at least one bit of bad news. One of the best adaptations — and perhaps the most underrated — is about to leave Netflix in just a few short weeks.

Castle Rock is set to be removed from Netflix on December 15th. That means that the last day to stream the series will be December 14th. The two-season, 20-episode series originally premiered on Hulu in 2018 but has been a hit on Netflix since it arrived last December. It’s a series that is not just great television, but truly unique as King adaptations go and if you haven’t seen it for yourself, you definitely should check it out before it says goodbye to Netflix.

While most adaptations of King’s work take on specific stories, Castle Rock is unique. The series takes on the larger mythology and lore of a larger world, specifically the fictional town of Castle Rock , Maine and the characters that are within the world that King has created. This setup allows the series to tell different stories and follow different characters, each one expanding on characters and stories that fans of King’s work already know. It’s a way to enhance things and it works beautifully.

The two seasons each tell different stories. Season one centers around criminal attorney Henry Deaver (Andrew Holland) who returns home to Castle Rock to represent a young man who is found in a cage at Shawshank Prison — The Kid. The season also stars Bill Skarsgard. Season 2 operates as a prequel to Misery and follows a young Annie Wilkes (Lizzy Caplan) who finds herself stranded in Castle Rock with her teen daughter Joy (Elsie Fisher) after a car accident. It’s a fascinating glimpse at a character fans have come to know as extremely terrifying and dark, but who is still disturbed even as a young woman, just in a different way. By building these backstories, the series creates a richness and nuance that elevates King’s work all while being a truly great television experience. It sadly only got two seasons, but they’re practically perfect and with just 20 episodes, it makes for an easy binge. Be sure to fit it in before the series leaves Netflix. It’s well worth the watch, even if you aren’t a fan of King’s brand of horror. These are just great characters and great stories – you can thank me later.

Castle Rock departs Netflix on December 15th.

articles.title: Demon Slayer Will Never Top Its Biggest Hashira Fight
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable Each season and movie of Demon Slayer has been exceptional without a doubt, but there's a reason why Mugen Train stands out as the best among them. The anime premiered in 2019, and only a year later, it released its first canon movie to continue Tanjiro's journey. The story completely changed from that point, and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Each season and movie of Demon Slayer has been exceptional without a doubt, but there's a reason why Mugen Train stands out as the best among them. The anime premiered in 2019, and only a year later, it released its first canon movie to continue Tanjiro's journey. The story completely changed from that point, and the major reason behind it was the fight between Rengoku and Akaza. As an action fantasy, Demon Slayer relies on intense battles, which are even further elevated in the anime. Ufotable has helped the series reach immense heights of popularity, all thanks to the exceptional adaptation and striking visuals.

Not only is the animation style one of the best in the industry, but the action sequences keep viewers at the edge of their seats. The series primarily centers around Tanjiro's journey, but the Hashira often end up taking the spotlight. As the nine most powerful Demon Slayers in the entire Corps, they often take on more challenging missions, especially where they have to fight the Twelve Kizuki. However, while dealing with the Lower Moons has always been easy for the Hashira, the Upper Moons are on an entirely different level. Akaza's appearance in the Mugen Train movie showed exactly what the Demon Slayers were up against, and that's what makes Rengoku's fight so iconic.

Akaza, the Upper Rank Three, completely overshadowed the main antagonist of the arc, Enmu, the Lower Rank One. Akaza only had a brief role in the arc, appearing after Enmu’s defeat. After realizing that Enmu had lost, Muzan Kibutsuji sent Akaza to the scene to get rid of the Demon Slayers, especially the Hashira. Akaza was only the Upper Rank Three at the time, which meant that there were three more villains stronger than him. However, the power he displayed was unlike anything viewers had ever seen. Without a Demon Slayer Mark, Kyojuro held his own against Akaza for a brief period, but the difference in their power was painfully clear.

Akaza didn’t even use all his abilities to defeat Kyojuro, one of the strongest in the Demon Slayer Corps. Realizing he was done for, Kyojuro used the last bit of his strength to keep Akaza from removing his arm so that he would be forced to stay in the open until sunrise. Akaza barely escaped with his life, but not before Tanjiro pointed out his cowardice and his defeat, which severely wounded his ego. The film already made Akaza one of the most popular villains thanks to his charisma and strength.

However, he gained even more popularity after the Infinity Castle Arc, which  unveiled his tragic past  and the reason he was so obsessed with power. In a way, both Akaza and Rengoku are considered similar yet fundamentally different from one another. While Rengoku desired power to protect the weak, Akaza wanted to be strong enough to crush those weaker than him. The film had many incredible moments, but Akaza’s debut could be considered one of the best not just in this arc, but in the entire series.

Rengoku died with a smile on his face, entrusting the future of the Demon Slayer Corps to the young fighters who looked up to him. Kyojuro had a strong sense of duty, and his desire to become strong was thanks to his mother’s dying wish for him to protect the weak. However, Kyojuro’s strength wasn’t what made him special; it was his fiery passion and the fact that he loved and valued the lives of everyone. He didn’t dismiss Tanjiro as weak but instead saw his true potential and didn’t allow Akaza to insult him.

In his final moments, he acknowledged Nezuko as a true member of the Demon Slayer Corps despite his initial dissatisfaction about a Demon Slayer traveling with a demon. He was barely holding on after controlling his breathing, but he only had a few minutes to live. He wanted to share his final words with Tanjiro, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira. After seeing their potential, Kyojuro wanted to encourage them to live with pride and not be overwhelmed by sorrow.

“Setting your heart ablaze” simply means having a strong desire to work towards one’s goal even in the face of adversity. His death was a reminder to the young slayers that they were truly too weak to protect everyone. His dying words sparked a new flame in the three up-and-rising Demon Slayers, who swore to continue moving forward, even if they were sad or filled with regret. They dedicated themselves to training and strived to become stronger, especially Tanjiro, who didn’t want to let anyone down as he did with Kyojuro. Tanjiro carried the guard of Kyojuro’s sword with him as a reminder of his determination and his desire to be like the Flame Hashira.

Do you think Demon Slayer has another fight that has a similar level of emotional impact? Or you can head down to the comments to share your favorite fight in the series.

articles.title: 5 Great Shonen Jump Manga Ended in 2026
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha 2026 was a major year for Shonen Jump fans, especially with the set of new releases and endings. When it comes to Shonen series, Weekly Shonen Jump always grabs the spotlight, and this has been the case for many decades now. Established in 1968, WSJ eventually became the best-selling manga magazine of all time. A lot of […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When it comes to Shonen action and drama, Weekly Shonen Jump always grabs the spotlight, and this has been the case for many decades now. Established in 1968, it eventually became the best-selling manga magazine of all time. A lot of its popularity is thanks to Dragon Ball, One Piece , and many other Shonen classics that kept the magazine running. However, while several of these classics received anime, not all of them got the adaptations they deserve. While the 2000s were a golden era for Shonen fans, many incredible anime suffered from poor pacing and cancellations.

The year is almost over, and Shueisha has already seen major changes in the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine and the official Shonen Jump+ platform. While the platform offers a wide range of series, WSJ has a rather limited lineup. Despite being serialized under the banner of Shonen Jump, a majority of the series don’t often get the attention they deserve and end up being cancelled. Manga series that aren’t performing well take up slots and incur losses to the publisher when the volumes get printed. This results in the series being discontinued abruptly, though unofficially, while some just reach their natural conclusion.

Yuki Kawaguchi’s Otr of the Flame made its Shonen Jump debut in May 2025, and after 34 chapters, it came to a close this January. Set in a world where the Ice Kingdom causes harsh, wintry conditions to persist, the story follows a cook who wishes to become a warrior — and gets the opportunity when the enemy arrives on his doorstep.

In terms of plot, the series has a lot of potential, but its pacing and execution never quite reach it. That’s a theme for Shonen Jump ‘s cancelled series of 2026, but the strength of this series’ artwork makes its fate especially tragic. It’s really a shame this one didn’t work out, but leave it to Shonen Jump ‘s first cancelled series of the year to hit the hardest. With a bit more direction, Otr of the Flame could’ve been a gripping ride.

The Jujutsu Kaisen manga reached its controversial ending in September 2024, leaving behind several unanswered questions. Only a year after the finale, Gege Akutami returned with a sequel manga that completely turned the world of Jujutsu Kaisen upside down. While Akutami served as the series’ writer, Yuji Iwasaki provided the gorgeous illustrations that fans can’t stop praising. The story takes place 68 years after the Culling Game, following new characters, including the grandchildren of Yuta Okkotsu, who were introduced in the epilogue.

The most shocking part of the sequel is how it explores sci-fi themes with aliens, also known as Simurians, who came to Japan as refugees. As the story continued, it focused primarily on the struggles between the sorcerers and the Simurians as their differences made it all the more impossible for them to co-exist.

Yuto Suzuki’s Sakamoto Days has now officially come to an end with Shonen Jump with the release of Chapter 284, six years after it originally made its debut. The series has been in the midst of its final arc for the past year, so fans have been preparing to say goodbye to the series for quite some time. But with many more fans assuming it would end earlier this Summer, the story was able to take its time and reach a more conclusive finale than many other Shonen Jump titles get .

Sakamoto’s dream of turning his convenience store into a franchise has also worked with a chain of stores across the region, and the final chapter reveals how each of the survivors (both friends and former foes) has since gone on to live new lives that don’t focus on killing. It’s a bright future for everyone as the world finds a new era of peace after everything that’s happened, and it’s clear that Sakamoto has indeed had an impact on everyone he’s come across through his time as a deadly killer.

Witch Watch Chapter 270 officially brings Kenta Shinohara’s long-running manga to an end after a year-long final arc that saw Morihito and the others taking on some very tough foes. The final chapter of the series moves ahead seven years and reveals what happened to everyone after the final battle. The group all decided to stay living together until after graduation, then went their separate ways after a while. Morihito and Nico ended up marrying and having a child together (who is nine months old by the time of the final chapter).

With Witch Watch creator Kenta Shinohara confirming that there will be some additional pages featuring more of the characters after the grand finale, it’s a hope that fans will get some of the closure they had been hoping to see that was absent from the final chapter. With it jumping years into the future, yet still teasing that all of the group would still be hanging out together, fans were hoping to just see more of the wacky adventures that drew them to the series in the first place.

The final few chapters of Black Clover wrapped up the long-running story fairly quickly and gave fans a suitable ending for Asta and many of the other characters as they moved into the future following the war against Lucius Zogratis. Though it’s now been confirmed that Tabata will be continuing the manga with a new special chapter coming later this August, so it’s time to try and figure out what kind of epilogue that Tabata is going to offer for the long-running series.

Black Clover is going to continue with an expanded ending after the release of its grand finale, and it’s time to get ready for what could be coming next. Yuki Tabata officially kicked off the final arc of Black Clover ‘s run a few years ago after it left the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine and moved to a quarterly release schedule where fans got to see a few chapters launched every few months. Wrapping up this final arc earlier this Spring, Black Clover ‘s manga ended after 11 years of serialization.

What are your thoughts on the finale of these Shonen Jump series? Do you hope that any of these have lasted longer? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Dragon Ball Super : Beerus is a huge disappointment after the Battle of Gods arc, which featured the main battle between Goku and Beerus. The anime returned this month as part of the Fall 2026 lineup, but instead of continuing the story with a sequel, Toei Animation released a remake version of the previous arcs. Since the anime returned after more than eight years, it’s no surprise that the hype was greater than ever, even if the new anime was a remake rather than a sequel. The biggest reason why fans were hyped over the anime’s return is that it aimed to fix the biggest issues with the original anime adaptations, including the animation quality and the pacing.

The remake is following the original story written by Akira Toriyama, the original manga creator, while also focusing on better visuals and fight choreography. A few episodes have already been out, and it’s obvious the new version is drawn from scratch instead of simply polishing the visuals. While the title is Dragon Ball Super: Beerus , the anime will retell the story of the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F, and Universe 6 arcs during its run. However, despite fan expectations, the remake isn’t as good as the studio claimed, and the third episode made it quite clear.

One look at the episode and you can tell easily  why it was flamed online by everyone. Not even the biggest fans of the anime could defend the third episode of the remake, and it’s really no surprise considering the rushed pacing and the jarring visuals. During the episode, Beerus arrived on Earth after crushing Goku on King Kai’s planet. However, Vegeta was there to keep things under control. King Kai had already warned him that the God of Destruction would be arriving on the planet, and it’d be best to avoid angering him. In order to save those around him and the planet, Vegeta was even willing to let go of his pride and do all the unnecessary jumping around, even if it made him look like a fool.

He served Beerus and Whis and did everything he could to make sure that none of the other Z Fighters would offend him in any way. Whether it was serving them a plate or dancing, Vegeta utterly humiliated himself in front of everyone. However, while some fans may think it was cringe or irrelevant, these moments highlighted how far he had come since his introduction. Someone as prideful as him was doing everything he could to save the planet, even if it meant bending to Beerus’ will.

As a child, Vegeta had already witnessed the horror Beerus invoked in those around him, which is all the more reason why those moments made sense and added to his character depth. However, most of those moments were original, which is why the anime removed them in the remake. Even so, there’s no denying that some of those added more to the character depth as compared to simply rushing things down and skipping over to the main battle.

It’s not just Vegeta, but the remake made every side character non-existent, which is a huge disappointment. The anime movie, Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods , was released before the Dragon Ball Super manga. While the movie didn’t actually follow the manga, it was already considered canon since the script and everything else was overseen by Akira Toriyama. Later on, the Battle of Gods was included in the manga for only four chapters, but the anime extended the arc with more scenes. The anime series highlighted the side characters even more, especially before Goku jumped into action. Not to mention that it also changed the moment where Beerus slapped Bulma.

Instead of hitting her purposefully, the remake showed that  Beerus accidentally hit her with his shoulder , which got Vegeta completely enraged. In the original anime, Vegeta tried his best to avoid a confrontation until he saw his wife being hit by the God of Destruction. Despite his fear and knowing he couldn’t win, he jumped straight into action, landing some of his most powerful attacks on Beerus. The remake was a great idea, but the execution was poorly handled. Some of the scenes remain the same while others changed completely. Not to mention that the visuals and filters aren’t as good as the anime promised, which is yet another major disappointment.

The anime had quite a lot of time to fix the issues with the previous versions, but it still didn’t change some of the drawings that needed corrections. While the remake was supposed to be a better version of the anime, at this point it’s pretty evident what fans prefer. Since the remake turned out to be a huge disappointment in only the first few weeks, there’s no denying that the next episodes will feature the same jarring color scheme and rushed pacing that completely took the heart and soul of the story away.

Do you think Dragon Ball Super: Beerus can turn things around later since the first arc has already raised concerns about how it will handle the biggest battles? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: You Can Get Your Hands on Margot Robbie's Harley Quinn Baseball Bat for a Price That Is No Laughing Matter
articles.summary: Courtesy of Warner Bros. There are some actors who take on roles they make their own and it becomes impossible for fans to see anyone else in the role. This is true of several stars that have become know for being the face of prominent comic book heroes and villains, such as Hugh Jackman as Wolverine or Robert Downey […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are some actors who take on roles they make their own and it becomes impossible for fans to see anyone else in the role. This is true of several stars that have become know for being the face of prominent comic book heroes and villains, such as Hugh Jackman as Wolverine or Robert Downey Jr. as Iron Man. Someone else who has found themselves in that same category is Margot Robbie , who made her debut as Harley Quinn in 2016's Suicide Squad and reprised the role again in Birds of Prey and James Gunn's semi-reboot, The Suicide Squad . While her future appearances are more up in the air than ever, fans can get their hands on Harley's famous baseball bat thanks to Heritage Auctions' latest memorabilia auction.

The item in question is the "hero" bat used for close-up shots in Suicide Squad and used by Robbie in several key moments in the movie. With the words "GOOD NIGHT" written across it in red, and several had-written lines, and taped handle, this is a grail item for any fan of either Robbie or her Batman villain counterpart. Although the bat comes with a starting bid of $12,000, you would be having a laugh if you thought that is what it will sell for. Back in March 2025, Prop Store sold a similar screen-used bat in one of their auctions which came with an estimate of up to $24,000 but ended up selling for $63,000. As the price of film memorabilia seems to only ever be increasing, it is likely that this sale will match that amount or push even higher.

Robbie's debut as Harley Quinn became one of the highlights of David Ayer's often criticized Suicide Squad , which was still a huge box office success earning over $749 million worldwide - the kind of gross that any recent DC movie would have loved to achieve and even Superman struggled to reach in 2025 despite being the big tentpole movie of the revamped DCU under James Gunn and Peter Safran. Robbie's scene-stealing maniacal performance was enough to get her a solo movie in 2020's Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn ) which managed to earn $205 million despite being impacted greatly by the COVID-19 pandemic . Quinn then returned again in James Gunn's own The Suicide Squad in 2021. While Gunn previously suggested that he fully expected Robbie to return again as Quinn , his departure from the DCU CEO role has now put this up in the air.

Regardless of Robbie's future as the character, her performance as Harley Quinn is one that is going to be remembered for a long time to come. For those who want something more than just her three movies, then this auction is going to make someone very happy with their new piece of the character's DCEU/DCU legacy if they can be the winning bidder in Heritage Auctions' sale. For everyone else, there are plenty of replicas out there that can be purchased for reasonable prices, they just don't come with the same kind of bragging rights that owning the real thing brings. For those interested in DC memorabilia, this is not the only lot available in the huge range on offer, with many Batman and Superman pieces also available including Val Kilmer's Batsuit and Christian Bale's Bat Pod vehicle which is expected to sell for somewhere in the region of $1 million. Compared to that, Harley's bat really is the cheaper option for collectors even if it will still break the bank for most people.

What piece of DC memorabilia would you love to own? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Ridley Scott's 10-Year-Old $630M Sci-Fi Masterpiece Is About to Land on a New Streaming Home in December
articles.summary: Courtesy of 20th Century Studios Although several of Ridley Scott's recent movies have been box office disappointments, that is not a reflection on the director's filmmaking. Films like Napoleon have recently struggled to get audiences into theaters despite being the kind of big budget spectacle that demands to be seen the big screen. 11 years ago, that was certainly not […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although several of Ridley Scott's recent movies have been box office disappointments, that is not a reflection on the director's filmmaking. Films like Napoleon have recently struggled to get audiences into theaters despite being the kind of big budget spectacle that demands to be seen the big screen. 11 years ago, that was certainly not the case when Scott directed a sci-fi survival movie that put Matt Damon on Mars and made a huge profit at the box office. The film was the highly acclaimed The Martian , which was released in 2015 to rave reviews and became one of the Alien director's best and most successful movies of the latter half of his career. Now, The Martian is finding a new streaming home on December 1, when it will join the Hulu library for a little while. Although it may not be the typical movie to get you in the Christmas spirit, it is a classic that does deserve to be watched while it is available.

The Martian tells the story of botanist Mark Watney, who finds himself stranded on Mars when his crew make an emergency departure from the planet during a violent storm, assuming him to be dead. However, he is very much alive, but not for long if he cannot find a way to survive in harsh conditions. While Mark fights the elements and depleting supplies, NASA attempts to work out how to rescue him and bring him home. The story is one of human spirit, the ability to continue in the face of overwhelming odds, and and uplifting, thrilling race against time movie that does not disappoint. Based on the novel by Andy Weir ( who was also behind Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary ), The Martian is a surprising movie for its unusual mix of comedy, drama, emotion and tension in equal measure.

Alongside Damon, The Martian packs in an all-star cast for it's reasonable $108 million budget. The ensemble includes Jeff Daniels, Jessica. Chastain, Kristen Wiig, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Sean Bean, Kate Mara, Sebastian Stan, and Mackenzie Davis. The talent on show is not wasted either, as not only did the movie land an astronomical $630 million worldwide gross as the 10th-highest-grossing movie of the year, but became Scott's higest grossing movie ever, easily passing decades old iconic classics such as Alien and Gladiator . That wasn't all, as the film also drew a lot of praise from both critics and audiences, with both rating the movie with a 91% score on the two sides of Rotten Tomatoes. Having identical scores is one thing, but having the same score at that level is something that doesn't happen too often.

The Martian 's mix of genres sparked an awards debate that has still to be resolved after all these years. Sparking controversy at the time, the film was submitted in the comedy categories of the Golden Globes, where it managed to win the Best Picture and Best Actor awards in the Musical or Comedy category. While many did not feel that the movie really sat in that category, it also received seven Academy Award nominations to show that regardless of the category, the film deserved the accolades it picked up. In recent years, the debate of what makes a movie fit the comedy category of several award has reared its head annually, around TV shows such The Bear as one example. For ayone who just loves movies, though, and doesn't pay much attention to that kind of thing, The Martian is a movie that can be enjoyed any time of year, but with it coming to Hulu in December, this year you could make Christmas a season of hope and optimism by putting the film on your watch list.

Is The Martian one of Ridley Scott's best movies? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Recasting the Original Pretty in Pink for 2026
articles.summary: One year after John Hughes’ iconic The Breakfast Club’s release, Brat Pack members Molly Ringwald and Andrew McCarthy starred in Pretty in Pink. Pretty in Pink centered on Molly Ringwald’s Andie Walsh, a high school senior navigating love and cliques. The movie is not without its controversies — the script originally called for best friends […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One year after John Hughes ’ iconic The Breakfast Club ’s release, Brat Pack members Molly Ringwald and Andrew McCarthy starred in Pretty in Pink. Pretty in Pink centered on Molly Ringwald’s Andie Walsh, a high school senior navigating love and cliques. The movie is not without its controversies — the script originally called for best friends Andie and Duckie to end up together before test audiences absolutely hated it, leading Andie to get with Blane in the end — but it has many of the charms of John Hughes’ other films , even if he didn’t direct it.

As a star and frequent collaborator with John Hughes, Molly Ringwald was instrumental to the film. Ringwald said she introduced Hughes to the Psychedelic Furs song that inspired Hughes to write the screenplay, and she had some influence in casting. The role of Andie’s love interest, Blane, could’ve gone to Charlie Sheen, but Ringwald convinced Hughes and Howard Deutch that Andrew McCarthy was a better fit. A third Breakfast Club castmate was also considered for Pretty in Pink, with Duckie almost going to Anthony Michael Hall. Hall turned it down, worrying about being typecast after playing the nerdy Brian in The Breakfast Club.

If recasting this iconic film for today, it is not only important to think about each individual actor but also how well they’d work together. Who has the potential — or has already proven themselves — to be a 2020s-era Brat Pack and bring Hughes’ original vision to life?

In terms of a leading lady for Pretty in Pink , Millie Bobby Brown definitely has it covered, already fulfilling that role in her various Netflix projects. While Stranger Things and the Enola Holmes franchise may be better received than Damsel or The Electric State, Brown’s star power is undeniable in all of them. Audiences have seen Brown believably play the outcast with Eleven, especially in the fourth season of Stranger Things when El and Will were sent to a new school, so the bullied Andie Walsh is hardly a stretch. Stranger Things is hardly the romantic showcase for Brown, but the more recent Enola Holmes films have leaned into romance between her character and Tewkesbury. Additionally, at only 22 years old, Brown is still young enough to believably play a high schooler.

Casting for the adult characters in remakes can be tough. Do you go for the instant nostalgia of trying to cast an actor from the original, but now in the role of the parent, or is it smarter to simply cast an actor who was active during that time period — thus still engaging that nostalgia factor without going for a 1-to-1 ratio.

A sweet spot for the character of Jack Walsh, played by Harry Dean Stanton in the original — who acted in nine films throughout the 1980s — would be Hugh Grant. Grant is a jack-of-all-trades and has no shortage of romantic comedy credits in his filmography, from Colin Firth’s romantic rival in the Bridget Jones series, a feature role in Love, Actually, and the male lead in Music and Lyrics in 2007. Grant also has no shortage of playing resentful and bitter, as his character Jack Walsh turns out to be when Andie finds out the truth about his “full-time job”.

Sorry to typecast Quinn-Toya as yet another guy who doesn’t — at least not yet — get the girl, but after seeing him in Amazon’s Sterling Point , he’d be great as Duckie. Toya’s character in Sterling Point, Rory, is a bit more vocal with his feelings but has no shortage of yearning, and even with being as communicative as he is, he can’t help but have a few stumbling blocks along the way. In the end, Rory doesn’t get the girl either, even though it takes him a while to realize it. 

With her father lying to her in the aftermath of the divorce, Andie Walsh needs another adult in her life for advice — she finds that in her thirty-something coworker/boss, Iona. In the original film, Iona was played by the actress Annie Potts. In a 2026 remake, she’d be played by Margaret Qualley. Iona manages the record store Trax, where Andie has an after-school job, and she encourages Andie to go to the dance even without a date. She even gives Andie her old prom dress for Andie to create something new from.

While Qualley may be better known for her serious roles, such as Netflix’s Maid and the horror film The Substance , she isn’t opposed to lighter fare. She’s shown a knack for comedy with Ethan Coen’s Drive Away Dolls and Honey Don’t! , and it is this comedic timing that can be utilized in Pretty in Pink with a quirky character like Iona.

I think enough time has passed since Stranger Things ended that I can say I never really bought into the chemistry between Mike and Eleven; I, however, do think it would be hilarious for Wolfhard to play aside Brown as a jilted not-lover. The character of Steff McKee is one of Andie and Duckie’s taunters, but finds Andie attractive and is still secretly resentful that she turned him down. Like Brown, Wolfhard is still in his early twenties and it isn’t out of the question to see him as a teenager, especially in a classic homage like a Pretty in Pink remake would be.

Are the Enola Holmes films good? That’s debatable. Are they entertaining? Yes. In the Netflix trilogy, Louis Partridge played Lord Tewkesbury, an unintended travel partner turned love interest to Millie Bobby Brown’s Enola Holmes. The pair are a delight to watch, and the chemistry’s believable even if the lines can veer dangerously close to cringey. Aside from casting for chemistry with leading lady Millie Bobby Brown, Partridge has definitely got that preppy charm down. He believably plays the type of guy who falls for the girl who’s different and who may falter at times but will stand by her in the end, the exact journey that Blane goes through in Pretty in Pink. 

Disagree with our picks? Think somebody else should’ve made the list? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Marvel Introduced the Hippest Mutants Ever in the Early '80s (and It's Long Past Time the MCU Made Them Superstars)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Marvel Comics is the biggest force in pop culture right now. Sure, their comics aren't selling as well as they once were and fans aren't exactly happy with them. On top of that, the Marvel Cinematic Universe isn't as popular as it once was. You'd imagine that it's not a great time to be the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics is the biggest force in pop culture right now. Sure, their comics aren't selling as well as they once were and fans aren't exactly happy with them. On top of that, the Marvel Cinematic Universe isn't as popular as it once was. You'd imagine that it's not a great time to be the House of Ideas, but this is not the case. Even though the company's fortunes are down, they've been able to position themselves as one of the most important tastemakers in pop culture. Marvel characters always have a chance to hit it big nowadays and there's one duo that should have been superstars ages ago – Cloak and Dagger .

It's not like Marvel hasn't tried with the characters; in 2018, they got a television series on Freeform. It's technically in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but it comes from that time when the canon status of the TV shows from the Disney family of pre-Disney+ networks was in question. Like the other Freeform shows, it had short time in the sun and then faded away. Meanwhile, in the comics, they haven't exactly been having a great time of things either. Cloak and Dagger have made several appearances lately , but they haven't been important in ages. With the two of them in Marvel Rivals , it's about time that Marvel remembers the duo that was meant to be the coolest new mutants of the '80s.

If you know anything about the '80s, you know that one of the defining features of the decade was fear-mongering involving children. It felt like the world finally realized how dangerous it was to children and suddenly, there were all kinds of cautionary tales about all of the bad things that could happen to your kids. These were the days "Just Say No", D.A.R.E., M.A.D.D., the "very special episode", the "after-school special", and the like. Cloak and Dagger fit perfectly into this world.

The two teens were first introduced in Peter Parker, the Spectacular Spider-Man #64 in 1982. Tandy Bowen and Tyrone Johnson were two runaways, living out on the streets and doing what they needed to survive. The two of them would get kidnapped by a gang and were experimented on with a new kind of drug. Instead of getting hopelessly addicted, the drug somehow tapped them into the source of light and darkness. Tandy would gain the power of light, allowing her to manifest light daggers and heal others and Ty's body was made into a link to the Darkforce Dimension, becoming a walking portal.

Another hallmark of '80s storytelling in general and comics in particular were creating this idea that all cities were dangerous places full of predators that only superheroes could fight. Cloak and Dagger would step up as defenders of the innocent, battling against the gangs that targeted them. The two quickly became fan-favorites in the Spider-Man comics, leading to a four-issue miniseries in the tail end of 1983. It was also a success, spawning a bimonthly ongoing series. Eventually, it would be combined with Doctor Strange to become a revival of Strange Tales , which lasted 16 issues before the they were split again, leading to The Mutant Misadventures of Cloak and Dagger , which ran another 19 issues.

Cloak and Dagger were created to be hip, cool new heroes and in the '80s, that meant one thing – mutants. The two of them, though, gained their powers from drugs. However, as their sales went down, Marvel decided that the best thing to do as a stop-gap measure was to establish them as mutants. Basically, the drugs they were given kickstarted their latent mutant abilities. On top of that, their powers were expanded; eventually, Dagger was linked to the very source of Light, becoming an avatar of it, while Cloak's Darkforce powers kept getting expanded.

However, as the years went on, Marvel could never really make the two work long-term. They were characters that everyone knew about, but they rarely showed up. They were '80s chic, in a lot of ways; by the '90s, they were mostly relics of another time. Teen heroes in the Marvel Universe in the Marvel Universe have been a tough sell for a while and the two of them were no different. Cloak and Dagger are part of that class of characters that everyone likes, but when they actually do get a book, it rarely sells. They're guest stars extraordinaire, basically.

However, it doesn't have to be that way. Cloak and Dagger have grown as characters over the years – even separating for a time – and it's about time that Marvel gave them another shot. Putting them in Marvel Rivals felt like a step in the right direction and it also gives the House of Ideas an example they can follow – Magik. Magik has been getting a lot of attention latel y; while the character has been consistently pushed for almost 20 years now, it's only been since Marvel Rivals that Marvel has been giving her a solo push.

Honestly, it would be very easy to do the same with Cloak and Dagger. They're mutants and Marvel is pushing the X-Men hard. While we don't really have a young mutant team, we do have some very popular young mutants in the Outliers and the Exceptional X-Men kids. They could use a mentor and Cloak and Dagger are perfect. It feels like Marvel is positioning the Outliers as new New Mutants and Cloak and Dagger would fit with them perfectly. Add in the magical connection of their powers, and you have two characters who are ready for the big time.

Cloak and Dagger have gotten one try in the MCU. However, it was the part of the MCU that no one really paid much attention to. The MCU has fallen from grace in recent years, but the excitement the debut of the X-Men is bringing shows that it still has its fans and still can be the biggest thing in pop culture. Cloak and Dagger being brought back with the rest of the mutants would be perfect and finally give them the chance they need to shine.

These two characters are so easy to make popular. Tandy and Tyrone are two great characters with awesome powers. They have a history with Spider-Man and the X-Men, and have played a role in more than one big story. The fact that they are such a hard sell in the 2020s is kind of depressing; sure, they are about as '80s as you can imagine, but they have that timeless quality that so much great '80s media has. The two of them could easily be made into the superstars they always should have been.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The franchise's co-creator Bryan Konietzko drops a major hint regarding future projects. The fan-favorite Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise keeps expanding as the latest animated series was released after 12 years to explore the unique worldbuilding and the captivating characters. Avatar: Seven Havens premiered in October this year and reached its conclusion in the same month. The first season wrapped up in Episode 13 before confirming that the animation series will return with sequel seasons eventually. While the journey of Pavi and Nisha will continue in Seven Havens , Avatar Studios continues to work on more projects for fans.

In an official Avatar: Braving the Elements podcast hosted by Dante Basco (the voice behind Zuko) and Janet Varney (the voice behind Korra), Konietzko discussed the immense hate Korra received when The Legend of Korra was released. Seven Havens takes place 225 years after The Legend of Korra , but it's obvious her story is far from over. Humanity not only blames her for the cataclysm, but also fears the Avatars for the powers they possess. While the second season of Seven Havens is expected to answer some burning questions regarding Korra , Konietzko has his own plans when it comes to this overhated character.

In a discussion regarding Korra, Konietzko shared, “If you don't like the series or you don't like the character, that's fine. If you don't like Korra because of misogyny, and just toxic internet garbage, then that's not fine.”

He also added, “Actually, that's a problem… You're not actually an Avatar fan. It's annoying, but it's also kind of what comes with any sort of success or popularity. You're just going to have these kinds of things.” Konietzko also revealed his plans for the future projects, “Here's the thing, I'm already two projects beyond what you're looking at. I'm working on something that you really don't want and you are not looking for, that I am so excited about.”

During the podcast, Konietzko didn't hold back his disappointment regarding the hate Korra has been receiving over the years. He also knows that there's some level of misogyny that's tied to the character's hate, which he is not happy with. Not to mention that Konietzko also doesn't consider Korra haters the fans of Avatar whose dissatisfaction with the character stems from misogyny rather than the way she is written. While fans are anticipating the return of Seven Havens , Konietzko confirms working on two more projects that haven't been announced.

And by the looks of it, both projects will have Korra as a crucial character. The Legend of Korra premiered in 2012 , centering around her life as someone born as Aang's successor as the Avatar. While her story was a massive hit, she is also one of the most polarizing characters in the series, with many viewers failing to appreciate her growth and character depth. After the recent podcast, it's evident Konietzko doesn't plan on holding back when it comes to having Korra at the center of attention for the next several years.

Seven Havens is the first animated series released since The Legend of Korra wrapped up, but the journey of Pavi and Nisha is far from over. Paramount is already working on a four-season series , which means fans can expect the story to continue for several years. While a second season was confirmed right after the first season's finale, there haven't been any updates on the release window. Fans have yet to get the first look at the second season as well, and there's no telling how long we will have to wait for it.

On the other hand, Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos was confirmed in October this year during the New York Comic Con. This animated series will serve as a prequel following the story of a 14-year-old Avatar Kuruk and his koala-otter companion, Nikik. The story will feature his journey as he rebels against tradition to master the four elements. Much about the series is still unknown, but judging by the premise and the first look revealed during this year's NYCC, fans can expect another banger from Avatar Studios.

What are your thoughts on Korra, and does she deserve the hate? Or you can head down to the comments to share your expectations for the future projects.

articles.title: Chris Hemsworth's 95-Minute R-Rated Meta Horror Movie Is One of the Most Creative Ever Made - and You Are Running Out of Time to Watch It
articles.summary: Courtesy of Lionsgate After more than a century of cinema, it is increasingly hard to surprise audiences. The horror genre is probably one of the toughest to be creative with, because even with all the monsters and demons you can imagine, every dark set of cellar stairs always lead to the same predictable jump-scares and dubious decisions. Yet […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After more than a century of cinema, it is increasingly hard to surprise audiences. The horror genre is probably one of the toughest to be creative with, because even with all the monsters and demons you can imagine, every dark set of cellar stairs always lead to the same predictable jump-scares and dubious decisions. Yet almost 15 years ago, one movie managed to cleverly pull the rug from under everyone by setting up a run-of-the-mill movie that turned out to be anything but. Starring Chris Hemsworth just before he became a Marvel star and action hero, The Cabin in the Woods even had a title that could make you roll your eyes at just how many tired paint-by-numbers horror tropes it was going to contain. That couldn't be further from the truth though, as the film instead delivered one of the cleverest and most re-watchable horror movies of the decade. Now fans only have a short time to catch it again before it leaves HBO Max on December 1.

The Cabin in the Woods certainly starts out as a movie you know you have seen before , which is partly the point. A group of college friends which includes Hemsworth's jock Curt, Kristen Connolly and Fran Kranz, head out to a remote - you guessed it - cabin in the woods. However, they soon find themselves under attack from a horde of monsters. What the audience soon discovers though is that this is not an ordinary cabin and these monsters are not what they appear. The cabin itself is part of a huge project which is being monitored by cameras and fed to a secret location where Richard Jenkins and Bradley Whitford's two technicians gleefully try to work out how to torment their targets next for a shady global purpose. What follows is a story that continues to unpack surprises right to the end, which is why it earned itself some rave reviews on its way to a moderately successful box office.

There are some movies that can be made or broken in Hollywood by events out of their control. The Cabin in the Woods did not blow the box office away - possibly because a lot of people did just think it was another same-old cheesy cliched horror flick - but was possibly helped to its $70 million success by something that almost prevented it from being released at all. The movie was originally shot for release in 2010, but around the same time as the movie was completed, MGM fell into a state of financial problems and The Cabin in the Woods was shelved, potentially to become a tax write-off if the need arose. Thankfully, Lionsgate eventually purchased the distribution rights for the movie and it premiered in 2012. While this could have been a bad thing for the movie, it turned out to be strangely helpful to the movie's promotion.

The original release date of 2010 would have seen the movie release before Hemsworth made his debut as Thor in the MCU , an event that really boosted his box office potential and did not hurt The Cabin in the Woods' 2012 release just weeks before The Avengers arrived in cinemas. We will never know how well the movie would have fared without this bit of adjacent promotion of Hemsworth's MCU outings, but one thing for certain is that The Cabin in the Woods did not just rely on that get by. The film is one of the most creative movies out there, and it is a great way to spend a lean 95 minutes. If you love a film that keeps you guessing about what is going to happen, then you could do worst that give T he Cabin in the Woods a whirl before it leaves its current streaming home on HBO Max.

Does The Cabin in the Woods deliver one of the best horror movies of the century? Let us know in the comments.

articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the finale of "Blade Runner 2099," now streaming on Prime Video. After discovering that the stolen memory they’ve spent the series searching for contains Dr. Eldon Tyrell’s (Joe Turkell) original Nexus-1 replicant […]
articles.content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the finale of " Blade Runner 2099," now streaming on Prime Video.

In the finale of " Blade Runner 2099 ," the future of humanity is anything but certain.

After discovering that the stolen memory they’ve spent the series searching for contains Dr. Eldon Tyrell’s (Joe Turkell) original Nexus-1 replicant design, Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (Hunter Schafer) face off against Julius (Sam C. Wilson), whose plans to create a new generation of replicants threaten to reshape the future of both humans and replicants. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Oscar Predictions: Costume Design — Will the Academy Embrace the Three Distinct Eras of ‘La Bola Negra’? Golden Globes: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Goes Comedy, ‘Dune 3’ Skips Box Office Achievement Category and More (EXCLUSIVE)

Olwen ultimately kills Julius, but not before he destroys the memory containing the secrets to his original design. In a final twist, Olwen, who was living out the last few days of her pre-determined lifespan as a replicant, discovers she has been transformed into a Nexus-1 herself and can now live the longer life she wished for. Meanwhile, Cora learns that Helena (Sheila Atim), the woman who raised her and Elias (Lewis Gribben), was a replicant, forcing her to reconsider everything she previously believed about humanity and explore the possibility that humans and replicants aren’t so different after all.

Elias, on the other hand, a more radical approach. Determined to fight back against the replicants and reclaim societal control as humans, he broadcasts a message to the population of Los Angeles falsely claiming responsibility for destroying the replicant birthing center in hopes of sparking a human uprising (Julius was the one responsible). But there is no rebellion. The replicants are still in control, and Elias’ fate is unknown. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Cora returns the LAPD, where she undergoes another Index test overseen by Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey) — a parallel to the premiere episode in which the results revealed she possesses no empathy, despite being a human. This time, however, Cora has developed empathy after learning to care for Olwen, who is now jetting off-world.

Below, "Blade Runner 2099" creator Silka Luisa breaks down the finale and what it means for the future of replicants in the "Blade Runner" universe.

Oh my gosh! What did you think? I’m so curious. What did you understand? What didn’t you understand?

Exactly. We had a lot of conversations about, “Should we change their costume? Should we make it clear who is what?” But what makes the world so unsettling is that you never really know, and I love that about the films. It was really important to us that you were never really on firm ground there.

That's so gratifying, because so many early conversations were had about how we make this accessible for people that haven't seen one of the films, both of the films or read the book. We had to find an entry point with original characters that you're also not going to have to catch everybody up to a bunch of lore.

Yeah. Sorry. At the end of the day, it's noir. It's not a revolution story, and that's why it was so important with the Elias storyline to give this sense of, “Is there going to be a rebellion? Is there going to be an uprising?” No. It's really just capitalism, and you're in a noir world where no one is coming to save you. This is the status quo, and you have to carve out your own future within these new circumstances.

Elias' story is about someone who is really just trying to find agency. At the beginning of the season, he’s taken care of by his sister, which is beautiful, but is very claustrophobic. And then he thinks that there's going to be some kind of uprising, and they're going to be able to recreate the world that once was. The truth is that that's not what's going to happen, and there's no one coming to save the day for him. While that is deflating, it's also an opportunity for him to falsely claim that he did this act of terrorism, because the truth is, if you want change in the world, sometimes you have to be the spark that ignites it. And it was really just trying to find a moment in the sun for him too, so that he could really be the change or be the hope for change that he wanted.

It's the same as with “[Blade Runner] 2049,” where I was like, “I think this is what happens four months later.” I’m sure everyone had different ideas. I obviously have my own story for each character and how I imagine it will continue, but there’s definitely a reason we cut the rope at the points we did.

That test has been an evolution through the films. In the first film, there's a void comp test, which is a straight up empathy test to tell the difference between replicant and human. In "2049," there's a baseline test, which measures emotional stability to see if you're able to be a police officer.

We've blended those, because now that replicants are policing the human population, there's a risk that they could develop empathy. If they develop empathy, it makes it harder to put intubating bags over them and police them, and you don't want that.

It was an important mirror scene to the end of the pilot, where she essentially passes that test, meaning she doesn't have any empathy. So she is a human who's just been stripped of her humanity, and I think that if empathy is the distinction between replicant and human, it's so interesting, because it is not definitive. It's something that you can gain or lose.

And at the beginning of this series, she lost it. Then at the end through this connection with Olwen, she rediscovers it.

Yeah. I think Cora has lost her own mother figure in Helena, and the surprise of the season for her is that she finds the surrogate mother in Olwen at the end.

I knew we wanted to end on a glimpse of off-world, which, if you're a fan, has been very mythologized. We wanted to give a little peek of what it could be, but trying to find some hope in the ending.

Exactly. And the endings of the films are ambiguous. They don't give you definitive answers, and there's been a lot of debate about both of them, even in the writers' room, about how we all understood certain final moments, which is always so much fun because I think that it just shows you that everyone is having an engaged and personal experience of the material. That was really what we were trying to strike that balance: how do we make this feel conclusive enough so that people know we have given them a true ending, but at the same time honor the films and leave enough questions for people to debate?

It's a tragedy, in this sense where they never get to have a forever ever together. She tells Cora to shoot on sight, and she does. And I think that she doesn't really believe him when he's saying why he left her. I wanted her storyline and her romance to actually be a very human romance. She's really a wounded lover who's been left in her final days, and she doesn't understand why. And the real emotional reason she's searching for answers is, she wants to understand why she was abandoned.

In the lore, they don't give you a lot of details about what Tyrell's original intentions were and the original different models. That always seemed intentional. So, when you think about Tyrell as a character, he's so grand in the first film, and he's such a dreamer. He seems so poetic. It just doesn't seem like he would have created these beings to be something small and just for labor, and that never really made sense to me from who he was. Those two things didn't seem like they fit, and so I was thinking, “What was his original intention when he made replicants?” He seems to have such a God complex. He would really want to create what comes next, the “next us.” And that is something that is better than us. It's not smaller. It doesn't have smaller lifespans. It's meant to go further. It's meant to extend far beyond.

No. The end of "2049" gives you the sense that there is a possibility of a mutiny brewing, and my own mind as an audience member was just like, "Oh, well, they're going to uprise." That's what I assumed happened, and so that was how I filled in the gap personally. And this is really just in the aftermath of what that would look like.

It's been part of the conversation for a couple years now, and I think it's obviously coming to a head with all of the AI debate, because we really are having a mirror held up to us, and we're starting to ask, “What is the value of humans? What can we do that nothing else can do? What is our purpose if we don't work right?” All these big philosophical questions are being forced upon us, so it's a really intense moment to be alive. Growing up, I never had this fear that humanity could ever end. That there would be a passing of the baton to something else, and it's been in the zeitgeist. That was definitely in my mind as I started the project.

If you're going to ask the question of, “What does it mean to be human?,” it does make sense to want to have more points of view on that, and that definitely felt like an addition to the conversation.

That was probably one of my favorite sets and sequences in the series. I just love the idea that, even though replicants have power, they still have this longing for what they can't have. It was so fun to build that out. We looked at a lot of real-world references from '70s New York and real peep shows, and the coin is taken from the real slots that they would have. There’s so many fun details in world building. You have this concept which is just prosthetics. How would you have that? How would you actually try and assimilate that in this kind of grungy underworld? The idea that you never get to grow old with someone is when Olwen emotionally realizes that her life has been cut so short.

This interview has been edited and condensed.
